mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which signals economic strength and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 4.5%, it indicates monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both real estate sentiment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) increase together, it signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If both RSAFS and HOUST increase but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) during an economic expansion signals strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases during expansion but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 grows but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200k but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is low and GDP (GDPC1) is growing, it indicates a supportive monetary policy for economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is low and GDPC1 grows but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary easing cycle signals lower borrowing costs, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.
